summary.headline: STL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 87% YoY to INR 1,910 crore, with EBITDA of INR 397 crore and EBITDA margin guidance raised to 23%.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR 1,910 crore (up 87% YoY), EBITDA INR 397 crore (up 184% YoY) and PAT a record INR 197 crore (10% of revenue). Q1 order inflow was INR 13,100 crore, including a $1.1 billion multiyear hyperscaler deal, and the open order book rose to INR 18,618 crore. The company became net debt-free after a INR 1,500 crore QIP, and management raised its FY27 EBITDA margin guidance from 20% to 23%. Management declined to give revenue guidance or disclose utilisation or segment margins.

financial_highlights.value: INR 483 crore; company described as net debt-free

financial_highlights.change: 1.7x total FY26 order wins of INR 7,687 crore

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,500 crore; 75% to debt reduction, balance to general corporate purposes

segments.name: Data Center
segments.commentary: Contributed 21% of revenue in Q1 FY27, up from 1% in FY26. Management expects combined Data Center and Enterprise to reach 50% of revenue this fiscal, versus 30% guided earlier.

segments.name: Telecom & Citizen Networks
segments.commentary: Described as a core pillar; the company did not give a separate revenue figure. Balance of the mix is expected to come from telecom and rural projects such as BharatNet.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North America 54% of revenue (39% in FY26), Europe 25%, rest of world 22%.

segments.name: Optical connectivity (attach rate)
segments.commentary: Attach rate rose to 16% on a larger OFC revenue base, versus 15% last year. Target is above 20% from next quarter and 25% by end-FY27. Revenue and EBITDA are not broken out.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance raised to 23% from the earlier 20%; management said margin gains will come from utilisation, product/customer mix and a higher cable-plus-connectivity ratio.
Data Center plus Enterprise targeted at 50% of revenue this fiscal, up from the 30% guided earlier; management said this is a directional mix and can vary quarter to quarter.
No revenue or full-year numbers guided; management said it does not guide revenue.
Q2 FY27 executable order book is INR 2,228 crore; INR 16,390 crore is scheduled for Q3 FY27 and beyond.
Capex of about INR 500 crore per year for three years (about INR 1,500 crore cumulative), covering equipment upgrades and debottlenecking.
Net debt-free status expected during FY27, supported by QIP proceeds, internal accruals and lower net working capital via shorter customer payment terms.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation not disclosed in absolute terms; management said it improved quarter on quarter and will keep improving.
Capacity is being added through equipment upgrades and debottlenecking across glass, fiber, cable and connectivity, to improve yields and output.
$100 million U.S. connectivity investment announced in May, spread over five years; it is connectivity capacity, not cable capacity. Management will update next quarter.
Neuralis portfolio supported by the South Carolina manufacturing facility in the U.S.; US Conec certification received for MMC pre-terminated solutions.
Management said it is taking orders with capacity availability in mind and picking and choosing orders.
demand_pricing: Q1 order inflow INR 13,100 crore, including a landmark multiyear $1.1 billion deal with a global hyperscaler for AI data center optical connectivity through FY29, plus multiple $100 million hyperscaler orders for high fiber count IBR cable.
Management said order inflow remained strong excluding the $1.1 billion deal; an analyst estimated about INR 3,000 crore ex-deal inflow, which management did not dispute.
Global ex-China OFC market share rose to 9%.
Management cited CRU forecasts: North America optical demand CAGR of 18.6% to 2030 (up from 15%), and 8.2% global cable demand growth in 2026.

Gross margin pressured by raw material costs (germanium, helium, polyethylene), which management linked to the conflict in the Middle East; management expects improvement and said polyethylene cost increases can largely be passed to customers.
Management declined to comment on realisations or pricing; it said the data center mix carries higher margins than telecom.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and whether data center ordering is still building?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose utilisation numbers but said it is improving quarter on quarter. It said hyperscaler multiyear capex continues, with about 8 to 10 GW of US data center build-out expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity take more large orders, and are capacity additions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in conversations with telecom and data center customers and is pursuing equipment upgrades and debottlenecking in parallel, which it expects to support further orders.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 revenue sustainable, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: No full-year or long-term guidance was given. Capex is about INR 500 crore per year for three years, cumulative about INR 1,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Germanium and helium supply, and their effect on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Germanium sourcing is being diversified and availability is expected to improve quarter on quarter; new technologies may cut germanium use. Helium is being recycled in part. Input cost rises are a margin headwind, which the CFO acknowledged.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt and working capital at FY27 year end?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company expects to be net debt-free during FY27, with QIP proceeds and internal accruals contributing, and that net working capital is being reduced by negotiating shorter customer payment terms.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company entering transceivers or semiconductors?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans for transceivers; focus stays on fiber, cable and connectivity. Semiconductors are not a near-term priority, though glass capability may be evaluated for some requirements.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation (germanium, helium, polyethylene) is weighing on gross margin; management said it expects improvement but gave no numbers.
Capacity constraints: management is now picking orders based on capacity, and utilisation is undisclosed.
Revenue concentration in a few large hyperscaler contracts; the $1.1 billion deal is multiyear through FY29.
Pace of the attach rate increase (16% to above 20% next quarter, 25% by FY27-end) and the 23% margin target depend on it.
Industry token-cost deflation in China and its possible effect on AI data center capex; management acknowledged the cost gap but remained optimistic on US capex.
Management did not disclose a breakdown of revenue or EBITDA between telecom and data center, or between optical connectivity and cable.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, orders and margins, backed by record reported numbers. Management was evasive on specifics: it declined to give revenue guidance, capacity utilisation, realisations, segment margins and germanium sourcing details, redirecting to qualitative answers.
key_quotes: We are now revising our EBITDA margin guidance upward to 23%.
In quarter 1 alone, we secured orders worth INR13,100 crores, which is 1.7x the total order wins of INR7,687 crores recorded in the entire financial year last year.
But we are very mindful and looking at improving our supply quarter-on-quarter.
